A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, title, and core experiments. All 40 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F, support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ensemble experiments on FairFace, UTKFace, and CheXpert, a controlled FashionMNIST experiment, and fairness-mitigation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds a controlled diversity experiment, subgroup-accuracy results, and calibration analyses by protected group.

M1.justification: Independent model training, prediction averaging, ensemble-weighting procedures, and Hardt post-processing remain unchanged. PP is renamed HPP. The additional synthetic experiment changes evaluation inputs, not the ensemble method.

E1.justification: All existing datasets and classification tasks are retained. Section 6 adds a distinct FashionMNIST input scenario: an image is concatenated with noise or an interpolation between noise and another same-class image. This extends controlled input conditions without adding a new domain.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain individual members, uniform ensembles, alternative ensemble weightings, and Hardt post-processing. Newly cited shallow-ensemble methods are discussed as related work, not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new controlled experiment sweeps interpolation coefficients 0, 0.2, 0.4, and 1 and evaluates an aggregate diversity score. Additional evaluations examine accuracy and calibration separately by group. Existing splits, training budgets, architectures, and post-processing validation procedures remain as documented in v1.

E4.justification: Section 6 adds a graded intervention testing whether increasing between-group predictive-diversity differences strengthens disparate benefits. New Appendix F.1 examines minimax fairness through subgroup accuracy, while expanded F.6 examines calibration within protected groups. These substantially extend the mechanism and fairness analyses beyond v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run reporting, uncertainty bands and numerical uncertainties, and Table 1's t-tests at p < 0.05. Added results do not introduce a different uncertainty-estimation procedure or establish an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds controlled-experiment results in Table 2, subgroup-accuracy curves in Figures 18–20, and subgroup calibration in Figure 29. Existing controlled-experiment curves and RegNet results also change: the reported FairFace age accuracy gain for RegNet is approximately 0.022 in v1 Figure 20 versus 0.031 in v2 Figure 24, under unchanged documented settings. Table 1 and the corresponding retained performance and post-processing tables have unchanged numerical entries.

T1.justification: Section 6 introduces a mathematical diversity score summing the absolute between-group DIV differences for the two target labels. The existing predictive-diversity definition, Bayesian derivation, fairness equations, and weighting formulas are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—disparate ensemble benefits, a predictive-diversity explanation, and effective Hardt mitigation—remain. However, v2's conclusion removes v1's explicit anticipation that the findings generalize to robust classification beyond socially salient groups, modestly narrowing the stated applicability.

C2.justification: Appendix F.1 adds the qualification that widening group disparities can coexist with improved accuracy for both groups, yielding improvement under a minimax fairness perspective. Section 6 interprets the graded experiment as further support for the diversity mechanism, and F.6 extends the calibration interpretation to individual groups. The principal vision-domain and fairness-metric limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new experiment's independent pixelwise noise and interpolation construction. Its acknowledgments newly identify the adapted error-parity package used for post-processing. Existing code-access information, hardware descriptions, and training-cost disclosures are retained; the package disclosure alone does not establish a procedural change.

R1.justification: Related work expands discussion of ensemble fairness through Kenfack, Gohar, Grgic-Hlaca, and Bhaskaruni, while Appendix F.1 introduces minimax-fairness literature. Appendix F.5 newly acknowledges the similarity of its retained weighting approach to Kenfack et al. The main positioning relative to Ko et al. remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits prose, changes PP to HPP, adds an Ensemble Fairness subheading, and introduces a separate Impact Statement that largely restates existing cautions. Section 6 and Appendix F expand, but the main section sequence and overall narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to an ICML two-column layout. Figure 1 moves to the first page, old Figures 4 and 5 merge, and new displays cover diversity controls, subgroup accuracy, and calibration. Many plots are redrawn. v2 Figures 9–11 introduce an inconsistency by plotting fairness-violation values while retaining '1 −' metric labels, unlike v1 Figures 8–10.

improvement.justification: The graded diversity experiment strengthens v1's existing mechanism evidence, and the minimax analysis usefully distinguishes worsening disparities from worsening outcomes for either group. Subgroup calibration also strengthens the mitigation discussion. These provide a limited net improvement, tempered by misleading axis labels in v2 Figures 9–11 and unexplained revisions to some plotted results.
